question: How is BlockSuite, the editor framework under `blocksuite/`, structured: what are its main packages and kinds of components, and how does the AFFiNE app use it?

points.text: BlockSuite has two groups of packages: a headless framework (`blocksuite/framework`: `@blocksuite/store`, `@blocksuite/std` and support packages) and the prebuilt editing components built on it (`blocksuite/affine`: the blocks, widgets, fragments, models and shared code); the framework does not depend on the components
`@blocksuite/store` is the data layer: documents are modeled on the Yjs CRDT, which gives them real-time collaboration and history (undo/redo)

`@blocksuite/std` (the docs' `block-std`) is the standard library for editable blocks: UI event handling, selection and clipboard (with commands), and the `EditorHost` that turns the block tree into components
rich text is handled by a small inline editor (the docs' `@blocksuite/inline`): each block's text is its own Y.Text with its own inline editor, instead of one rich-text editor for the whole document

its component types are editors (the page editor and the edgeless whiteboard editor), blocks, widgets (helper UI that shows up for a block, such as the slash menu or drag handle) and fragments (UI outside the editor that shares its document, such as the doc title or outline panel)
all of these components are native web components built with lit, while the AFFiNE app is written in React, so the app wraps BlockSuite's editors in React components

an editor is thin, just the set of block and widget registrations mounted on an `EditorHost`; so the page and edgeless editors are two views of the same document, and the root block keeps one model (`RootBlockModel`, flavour `affine:page`) with a different view in each
BlockSuite stands apart from the app, like Monaco from VS Code: the app depends on BlockSuite and reuses it through its components, and BlockSuite never imports the app's code

answer:
BlockSuite lives in `blocksuite/`. I read the folder layout and the descriptions of each folder. I didn't open the source files, so the AFFiNE integration part is based on folder names and import counts.

**Framework (`blocksuite/framework/`)** has four core packages:
- `global`: shared utilities.
- `store`: the Yjs-backed document model, meaning blocks, schemas and transactions.
- `sync`: syncing.
- `std`: the runtime for block views, selection, commands and the canvas (gfx).

**Affine feature layer (`blocksuite/affine/`)** builds on the framework. It has these kinds of components:
- **`blocks/`**: block types such as paragraph, list, code, note, database, table, image, attachment, bookmark, embed, frame, latex, callout, divider, edgeless-text, surface, surface-ref and root.
- **`model/`**: block and element models.
- **`gfx/`**: edgeless-canvas elements and tools: brush, connector, group, mindmap, shape, text, template, pointer, note, link and turbo-renderer.
- **`widgets/`**: UI overlays such as the drag handle, slash menu, toolbar, keyboard toolbar, linked-doc, remote-selection, and the edgeless toolbar and zoom toolbar.
- **`inlines/`**: inline features such as reference, link, mention, footnote, comment and latex, plus a preset.
- **`fragments/`**: side panels such as outline, frame-panel, adapter-panel and doc-title.
- **`rich-text/`, `components/`, `shared/`, `foundation/`, `data-view/`**: shared building blocks and UI.
- **`ext-loader/`**: an extension loader.
- **`all/`**: an aggregate package that bundles everything.

**Tooling and test folders:** `playground/` (a dev playground), `integration-test/` (a browser-based test harness), `docs-site/` (a VitePress documentation site) and `docs/`.

Almost everything is an extension. Blocks, widgets, inlines and gfx elements each ship their own store and view extensions. `std` collects those extensions into an editor.

**How AFFiNE uses it:**
- `blocksuite/` doesn't import anything outside itself.
- It is imported by `packages/` (about 1,097 imports), `tests/` (74), `scripts/` (1) and `tools/` (1).
- The main consumer is the frontend core, `packages/frontend/core/src/blocksuite/`. It has these subfolders:
  - `block-suite-editor`, `editors`, `block-suite-header`, `block-suite-mode-switch`, `block-suite-page-list` and `outline-viewer`: the editor and its surrounding UI.
  - `view-extensions` and `store-extensions`: AFFiNE's own extensions, which it registers on the editor alongside the stock ones from `blocksuite/affine`.
  - `manager`, `initialization`, `ai` and `database-block`: setup and app-specific features.
  - `attachment-viewer`: a viewer for attachments.
- The `ext-loader` package is imported about 25 times under `packages/frontend/core/src`. I believe that's how AFFiNE registers its extensions, but I didn't confirm it.

In short, AFFiNE doesn't fork the editor. It composes BlockSuite packages and adds its own extensions, such as AI and workspace-specific behavior.
